transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-16
Start: 15:34 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramirez (Redwood SE), Ethan Moore (Novum - Head of Procurement), Priya Shah (Novum - Legal), Dr. Lena Ortiz (Novum - CTO)

Summary:
- Review of MSA and DPA redlines, discussion of SLAs and onboarding steps for pilot.
- Security questions around data residency, KMS, SOC 2, audit logs, and SSO.
- Pricing approval process and PO timeline clarified; next steps to send redlines and schedule kickoff.

Topics:
- MSA terms and indemnity, liability caps
- DPA, data processing, encryption/KMS, data residency
- SLAs, uptime, support tiers, incident response
- Pricing approvals, PO timing, pilot scope and success criteria
- Onboarding timeline and required tech contacts

Action items (captured in metadata above).

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we're just gonna run through the ms a and dpa and then go through the onboarding ask and timeline. uh diego will jump into the technical bits after the legal points.
[00:18] Ethan Moore: thanks Maya, appreciate it. we only have about 50 minutes so, um hopefully we can get to the redlines. Priya has the doc open.
[00:28] Priya Shah: yes I have it, okay, um first point is section 7, liability caps - our legal ops wants to keep a reciprocal cap for data breaches. currently your version has a vendor-only cap. can we make that reciprocal?
[00:45] Diego Ramirez: yeah, so the standard redwood template tends to be vendor-liability capped, but we can discuss reciprocal language. i can say from an operational standpoint we have SOC 2 and a number of controls in place - but i'll let maya speak to commercial flexibility.
[01:05] Maya Chen: absolutely. on cs side we are open to discussing reciprocity in material ways for enterprise deals; we'll need to align with finance for specific cap numbers. do you have a target cap you want to see, Priya?
[01:18] Priya Shah: ideally something tied to fees for 12 months, or a fixed minimum of 1M. i can propose language.
[01:26] Maya Chen: that's reasonable; we'll take that back and propose alternate language in the redline.
[01:34] Dr. Lena Ortiz: quick question on data residency - our research subsets contain EU and US patient metadata. we need to ensure PII stays in region. how does Redwood handle data residency and VPC/private deployments?
[01:47] Diego Ramirez: good question. so we support private deployments and VPC peering - you can either run in our hosted regioned model where data stays in region, or we can do dedicated/private with customer-managed VPC. there are, um, some deployment steps to ensure keys and logs stay behind your network.
[02:10] Ethan Moore: is that an additional cost? procurement will need to know.
[02:15] Diego Ramirez: dedicated/private usually has a reserved capacity charge; pricing's on the spreadsheet but typically it's a monthly commit. for strict data residency we recommend dedicated or private. hosted can be region-restricted but we don't do per-tenant physical isolation there.
[02:32] Priya Shah: and on encryption - do you let customers bring their own key (BYOK) / KMS? we need HSM-level controls for certain workloads.
[02:42] Maya Chen: yes, BYOK via KMS integrations is supported for Private customers; for Dedicated we also support customer-managed keys in supported clouds and HSM integrations for on-prem bundles.
[02:55] Priya Shah: okay good. can you share the KMS integration doc?
[02:58] Maya Chen: absolutely we'll send the security pack link after the call.
[03:06] [03:06] Ethan Moore: jumping back to the dpa - data subject rights and delete requests, how long does redwood keep logs and telemetry? we need deletion timelines.
[03:18] Diego Ramirez: default retention is 90 days for request telemetry but we can offer custom retention for enterprise plans and for private customers you control the retention. there's also an option to purge KV cache snapshots on demand.
[03:33] Priya Shah: let's note that as a required clause in the DPA.
[03:36] Maya Chen: noted. we'll propose clause for retention, purge, and confirm controls for deletion.
[03:42] [03:42] Dr. Lena Ortiz: there's also a performance question - our inference workloads are sensitive to latency. can you guarantee token latency for the pilot? we need something like p95 under 150ms for short prompts.
[03:56] Diego Ramirez: for short prompts, on dedicated pools we can typically hit p95 sub-100ms depending on model and batch tuning; on hosted it depends on instance and load. for pilot we recommend a small dedicated pool to ensure stable p95 and then scale. we can run a bench with your sample prompts.
[04:19] Ethan Moore: procurement needs numbers to justify the cost. can you provide benchmark sheet and a sample invoice for dedicated pilot?
[04:27] Maya Chen: yes we'll share the model performance spreadsheet and a pricing estimate for a 3-week pilot.
[04:33] Priya Shah: SLAs - uptime and credits. the MSA mentions a 99.9 uptime with credits; is there a higher tier for 99.95?
[04:42] Diego Ramirez: we have SLA tiers for Dedicated; 99.95 is available under premium SLA with a price adjustment. uptime is monitored via console and we provide incident reports and postmortems for Sev1s.
[04:55] [04:55] Ethan Moore: how about incident response times? we require a 1-hour acknowledgement for Sev1s during business hours.
[05:03] Maya Chen: we have 1-hour initial response for Sev1 under enterprise support add-on; we can include that in the enterprise attachment.
[05:10] Priya Shah: good. can you also confirm audit log retention and access for our auditors? they will want read-only access to logs for compliance reviews.
[05:20] Diego Ramirez: yes, we support audit log exports and can set RBAC with read-only roles and SAML/SSO to integrate with your identity provider.
[05:29] Dr. Lena Ortiz: speaking of SSO, we use Okta. how's the SAML flow?
[05:34] Maya Chen: full SAML SSO is supported - we'll provide SAML metadata and a guide.
[05:40] [05:40] Ethan Moore: quick procurement admin question: what's the typical time from signed MSA to onboarding kickoff? we need to plan resource windows.
[05:47] Maya Chen: typically 2 weeks - assuming PO/contract signature and security review cleared - pilot kickoff can happen within 7-14 days.
[05:55] Priya Shah: and for PO approvals, our CFO needs a clear pricing sheet. can you break out reserved versus usage costs?
[06:03] Maya Chen: yes we'll provide a line-itemed quote - reserved capacity, burst charges, and overage rates.
[06:09] [06:09] Diego Ramirez: for the pilot we suggest reserved for the pool and usage billing for spikes; we can show cost models for different p95 targets.
[06:19] Dr. Lena Ortiz: sample data flows - Diego can you outline what telemetry we send to Redwood and what stays local if we choose private? we need to make sure PII never leaves our environment.
[06:31] Diego Ramirez: in private/on-prem, you control the entire env including logging. with dedicated managed by Redwood we still collect operational metrics but can anonymize or redact sensitive payloads and route logs to your syslog endpoint on request.
[06:45] Priya Shah: ok we will add a requirement to the dpa on redaction and log forwarding.
[06:50] Maya Chen: understood, we'll add that to redline.
[06:54] [06:54] Ethan Moore: any competitors concerns? our infra team looked at Anthropic and Bedrock. cost on Bedrock was higher for identical latency.
[07:03] Maya Chen: we've seen that; our focus is cost-performance and operational predictability - we'll include comparative notes.
[07:11] Priya Shah: about indemnity for third-party data, we need wording that covers research datasets we license.
[07:21] Maya Chen: we'll propose language that ties indemnity to misuse and not licensed dataset obligations; legal can refine.
[07:30] [07:30] Diego Ramirez: technical onboarding notes - we'll need a list of sample prompts, expected qps, and a short runbook for model selection; i'll prepare a pilot runbook with steps for validation.
[07:43] Dr. Lena Ortiz: i'll get that to you by Monday.
[07:46] Ethan Moore: procurement timeline: CFO signoff target is 6/30. that means we need final redlines and pricing by 6/24 ideally.
[07:55] Maya Chen: great - timeline noted, we'll target redline delivery by 6/19 and pricing by 6/21.
[08:03] Priya Shah: regarding DPA subprocessor list - can we get the list of subprocessors and the way you manage changes? we need a 30-day notice on any new subprocessors.
[08:14] Diego Ramirez: yes we'll provide current subprocessor list and commit to notice on changes; for enterprise customers we can do contractual notice periods.
[08:24] [08:24] Ethan Moore: onboarding docs and security pack would be helpful for our InfoSec review. can you share those links in the follow-up?
[08:31] Maya Chen: yes, will send security pack and SOC 2 report link.
[08:36] Maya Chen: quick follow-up on pricing approvals - Ethan, does procurement need an example invoice or PO line items?
[08:42] Ethan Moore: invoice example yes, and a short T&C summary for our finance team.
[08:48] Maya Chen: we'll include that.
[08:51] [08:51] Priya Shah: a small nit on the MSA: termination for convenience notice period - can we change 90 to 60 days?
[08:58] Maya Chen: we can propose 60 days for enterprise deals but need to confirm with finance; we'll include that in the redline.
[09:06] Dr. Lena Ortiz: security question - how do you handle model hallucination risks for PHI? any guardrails?
[09:15] Diego Ramirez: we have output filters, rate limits, and model selection and can run safe-token policies; for PHI we recommend extra validation steps and domain-specific evals. part of the pilot will be quality checks tied to your eval prompts.
[09:35] Ethan Moore: final thing - onboarding training for our devs; do you provide a short workshop?
[09:41] Maya Chen: yes we do a 2-hour tech onboarding and a 1-hour ops session as part of the kickoff.
[09:48] Priya Shah: great.
[09:50] Maya Chen: ok to recap real quick: 1) we will send redlined MSA/DPA (target 6/19), 2) share SOC2/security pack and KMS docs, 3) pricing estimate and sample invoice (target 6/21), 4) schedule onboarding kickoff week of 6/22 pending signatures, 5) Diego will deliver pilot runbook and benchmark notes. any changes?
[10:15] Ethan Moore: that lines up. thanks everyone.
[10:20] Dr. Lena Ortiz: thanks.
[10:22] Priya Shah: thanks.

End of transcript.
